paragraphs: The paper asks whether large language models can help predict how social beliefs change after events. Its Social World Model represents beliefs as a changing state and learns transitions between states. The goal is to connect events with subsequent belief dynamics using patterns in social data, drawing on the commonsense and social knowledge available in language models.

Training mines temporal relationships and optimizes an evidence lower bound, an objective used to learn probabilistic models. This approach avoids requiring people to explicitly label which events caused particular belief shifts, and it does not require expensive census data. The contribution is therefore both a modeling framework and a way to learn it from less explicitly annotated observations.

The authors introduce SWM-bench, containing more than 12,000 prediction examples from Kalshi and Polymarket across politics, finance, and cryptocurrency. SWM significantly outperforms time-series foundation models, reaches state-of-the-art results on Kalshi, and is competitive on Polymarket. These findings support its usefulness for the benchmark’s market-derived belief predictions, alongside interpretable accounts of the modeled dynamics.
icml-2026-building-social-world-models-w.tldr: Social World Models learn how beliefs change around events and achieve strong prediction results on a benchmark derived from prediction markets.

paragraphs: A model can perform well during training by relying on a relationship that later changes. The paper studies a specific source of this problem: hidden variables that create misleading associations between inputs and outputs. For example, a text model may associate a particular data source with positive sentiment, then fail when that source contains mostly negative material.

Causal Fine-Tuning introduces a structural causal model to guide what the learned representation should separate. The authors derive sufficient identification conditions that motivate dividing representations into stable, high-level components and lower-level components that are sensitive to shifts. These conditions support the proposed objective; they are not presented as conditions that every successful adaptation method must satisfy.

The framework is implemented in BERT, where learning and adjusting the causal and spurious components produces a more robust predictor. Experiments involving injected spurious correlations in text outperform black-box domain generalization baselines. The findings support explicitly representing causal structure when adapting to this kind of shift, with the reported evidence coming from the studied text attacks.
icml-2026-causal-fine-tuning-under-laten.tldr: Causal Fine-Tuning separates stable and shift-sensitive representations to improve robustness against misleading correlations in text.

paragraphs: Prediction intervals express uncertainty by giving a range for a future value. For time series, the relevant distribution can change over time, making interval calibration difficult. Existing sequential conformal methods can produce unstable boundaries, especially when estimating distribution tails. Different requested confidence levels can also yield intervals that cross rather than fit consistently inside one another.

Conditional Quantile Adjusted Conformal Prediction addresses these problems by modeling a whole conditional quantile curve for nonconformity scores, which summarize prediction mismatch. At each step, it evaluates a base learner at several quantile levels. It then fits a Cornish–Fisher approximation using conditional moments and monotonicity constraints, imposing structure on the estimated curve instead of treating each quantile independently.

The authors prove asymptotic conditional validity under serial dependence and establish improved conditional quantile estimation accuracy. The validity result concerns limiting behavior, rather than an unconditional finite-sample guarantee. Across real-world datasets, the method maintains accurate coverage while producing smooth, narrow, nested intervals across significance levels and prediction models. These results indicate more coherent uncertainty estimates as the requested confidence level changes.
icml-2026-conditional-quantile-adjusted-.tldr: CQACP stabilizes time-series prediction intervals by fitting a structured, monotone conditional quantile curve.

paragraphs: Offline meta reinforcement learning uses recorded experience from multiple tasks to train a policy that can generalize to unfamiliar tasks. Extending this idea to teams introduces two difficulties. An individual agent has limited access to global information, making the team’s task harder to identify, and knowledge transfer can suffer when the agent’s role is not represented.

D²TR learns separate representations for the shared task and individual roles. For task identification, mutual-information knowledge distillation aligns representations available to decentralized agents with centralized representations inferred from global trajectories. This provides a training route for transferring team-level information into representations that agents can infer using their more limited observations.

For role identification, a large language model assigns semantic roles to trajectories in the offline dataset. Agents then learn decentralized role representations from that information. Across CN, SMAC, and SMACv2, D²TR generalizes strongly to unseen tasks and outperforms the evaluated multi-task and context-based meta reinforcement learning baselines. The results support treating team context and individual responsibility as distinct sources of information for transfer.
icml-2026-decentralized-and-disentangled.tldr: D²TR separates team-task and individual-role representations to improve decentralized agents’ generalization from offline experience.

paragraphs: Reading text in images requires preserving small visual details that high-level semantic reasoning may overlook. The paper identifies a training problem in models that combine features from several visual layers. Skip connections let early visual features reach later processing stages, but they also create direct routes for gradients from semantic objectives to alter those early layers.

Detached Skip-Links retain the useful forward flow of shallow features while stopping gradients through the skip branch during joint training. This separates feature reuse from one source of optimization interference. The modification adds no learnable parameters, and the authors report improved training stability and convergence as low-level visual signals face less disruption.

The paper also introduces R-Probe to test whether projected visual tokens preserve detailed information in a form usable by the language model. A shallow decoder initialized from the first quarter of its layers measures pixel-level reconstruction. Across multiple vision-transformer backbones, multimodal benchmarks, and training scales up to seven million samples, the approach consistently improves OCR-focused results and also benefits general multimodal tasks.
icml-2026-detached-skip-links-and-r-prob.tldr: Detached Skip-Links preserve useful visual features while blocking interfering gradients, improving OCR and broader multimodal performance.

paragraphs: FormAct treats document generation as an iterative editing process. Producing a professional document requires both useful content and a successful rendered layout, so the system works with an HTML source representation and repeatedly improves it. Its workflow connects changes to the underlying document with feedback about how the resulting pages actually look.

An editing agent uses tools that include a syntax-aware source editor and a template retriever. A separate review agent examines rendered pages and critiques them to guide subsequent revisions. Edit-triggered context compression keeps the working context bounded as these rounds accumulate, supporting efficient continued editing rather than requiring the entire interaction history to remain active.

The authors also introduce two evaluation resources with different purposes. RichDocBench measures generation from start to finish, while RichDocFuzz tests whether reviewer agents recognize formatting errors. Automated evaluations and blind human-preference studies show consistent improvements over strong baselines, including Codex-CLI. The strongest reported gains concern producing professional documents without formatting errors, supporting the combination of source editing and visual review.
icml-2026-formact-agentic-source-editing.tldr: FormAct combines HTML editing, rendered-page review, and context compression to generate more polished rich-format documents.

paragraphs: Many time series contain observations taken at uneven intervals, even though the underlying system evolves continuously. Modeling these data requires connecting sparse, asynchronous measurements to continuous dynamics. Existing continuous–discrete state-space methods often perform inference over entire paths, which can be computationally expensive or depend on restrictive assumptions about the inferred distribution.

SDEVI instead performs variational inference directly over the joint distribution at discrete observation times. Its construction guarantees consistency with an underlying continuous process governed by a stochastic differential equation. This keeps the continuous-time foundation while moving inference toward the observations that are actually available. Linear time-varying stochastic differential equations induce the variational posterior used as its scalable backbone.

To represent more intricate dynamics, the authors introduce inference induced by nonlinear stochastic differential equations and extend the framework to the complex domain. Experiments cover healthcare, physics, climate, and Internet of Things benchmarks. The reported state-of-the-art results span interpolation, extrapolation, regression, and classification, indicating that the framework supports several uses of irregularly sampled data rather than a single prediction setting.
icml-2026-generative-modeling-of-irregul.tldr: SDEVI models irregular observations directly while preserving consistency with continuous stochastic dynamics.

paragraphs: Constraint-based causal discovery uses conditional independence tests to help identify relationships between variables. These tests become less reliable when they must account for many other variables at once. The problem is particularly acute around highly connected hub nodes. Restricting possible edges or global graph structure does not necessarily control the size of each test’s conditioning set.

Ordering-Constrained Markov Blanket discovery makes that size an explicit design constraint. It first estimates a lightweight global ordering that provides directional guidance. It then validates local relationships within small candidate sets restricted by that ordering. Applying directional constraints before the independence tests keeps conditioning sets bounded even when the graph contains hubs.

The theoretical recovery claim depends on a high-recall ordering assumption: under that assumption, OCMB recovers correct parent sets without needing a globally correct ordering. This makes the quality required of the preliminary ordering central to the guarantee. Experiments show significantly improved precision and robustness over constraint-based and hybrid approaches in high-dimensional settings where conventional independence-testing methods fail.
icml-2026-global-directional-priors-with.tldr: OCMB uses approximate global ordering to keep local causal tests small, with parent recovery guaranteed under a high-recall ordering assumption.

paragraphs: Sampling methods often work with a probability distribution whose normalizing constant is unknown. This paper addresses a harder situation: evaluating even the unnormalized distribution is expensive or infeasible. Examples include Bayesian inference with very large datasets and doubly-intractable distributions. In these settings, avoiding the normalizing constant alone does not remove the main computational obstacle.

The authors identify a common procedure underlying several existing Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms, including the exchange algorithm, PoissonMH, and TunaMH. They extend that procedure into a framework that allows auxiliary variables in both proposal generation and the acceptance–rejection decision. This creates a shared way to design algorithms whose sampling steps do not require direct target evaluation.

Several resulting algorithms use estimated gradients to guide proposed moves. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets show significantly better performance than existing methods. The paper also develops theory for the framework and uses it to simplify and extend results for earlier algorithms. Its contribution therefore combines a unifying explanation of existing techniques with new, empirically stronger sampling methods.
icml-2026-markov-chain-monte-carlo-witho.tldr: An auxiliary-variable framework unifies existing MCMC methods and enables improved gradient-guided sampling without directly evaluating the target.

paragraphs: Multimodal language models can produce reasoning that is vulnerable to misleading cues or fails to distinguish between different rationales. MIND addresses these problems by organizing learning around understanding, reconsideration, and correction. The aim is to train models to discriminate between reasoning paths and repair logical problems, rather than relying only on imitation of demonstrated answers.

The framework begins with Rationale Augmentation and Discrimination, which supplies a unified, extensible data foundation. Its Progressive Two-stage Correction Learning strategy then separates two training purposes. The first phase strengthens learning from multiple positive rationales, while the second develops active logical discrimination and correction. This sequence gives reasoning acquisition and reasoning revision explicit roles in training.

MIND also uses Multi-rationale Contrastive Alignment to reduce entanglement among representations of different rationales. This component addresses how reasoning alternatives are organized internally, complementing the data and correction-learning components. Experiments achieve state-of-the-art performance on multiple public datasets. The reported results support the overall framework’s effectiveness for multimodal reasoning, while its human-like terminology describes the intended workflow rather than establishing human-equivalent cognition.
icml-2026-mind-multi-rationale-integrate.tldr: MIND trains multimodal models to learn multiple rationales, distinguish logical errors, and correct their reasoning.

paragraphs: Agents that operate user interfaces need enough information to choose and ground their actions. Sending an entire interface state to a remote model can also expose unrelated private material, such as authentication codes or notifications. MINIM places a trusted broker on the client device to reduce the observation before any of it is transmitted.

For each interface element, the broker predicts two scores: how sensitive the element is inherently and how necessary it is for the current task. A three-way policy then retains essential elements, abstracts sensitive attributes when needed, or removes irrelevant content. The distinction between sensitivity and necessity allows disclosure decisions to depend on both the information and its purpose.

Training follows a Contextual Integrity objective that penalizes necessity errors more strongly for high-risk content. This supports aggressive pruning while retaining information needed for the task. Experiments using real-world interface observations derived from WebArena substantially reduce irrelevant sensitive leakage while preserving task-critical meaning and interactive affordances. The findings support minimizing what remote agents receive without discarding the interface cues their actions require.
icml-2026-minim-privacy-aware-minimal-vi.tldr: MINIM locally filters interface observations according to sensitivity and task necessity, reducing irrelevant private disclosures.

paragraphs: MME-Reasoning evaluates logical reasoning in multimodal language models across three categories: induction, deduction, and abduction. These correspond to drawing general patterns, deriving conclusions from premises, and inferring explanations. The benchmark responds to evaluations that lack explicit reasoning categories, making it difficult to tell whether strong results reflect broad reasoning competence or strength in a narrower subset.

The authors curate questions to target reasoning rather than visual perception or breadth of factual knowledge. They also extend evaluation protocols to accommodate diverse questions. This design matters because successful multimodal answers can depend on several abilities at once; clearer question construction helps make reasoning itself the focus of the assessment.

The evaluation finds substantial limitations even among the strongest tested models, along with pronounced differences in performance across reasoning types. The paper also examines thinking modes and rule-based reinforcement learning, approaches commonly associated with reasoning improvements. Its central finding is that comprehensive assessment reveals uneven capability, motivating attention to the full range of logical reasoning rather than only selected forms.
icml-2026-mme-reasoning-a-broad-spectrum.tldr: MME-Reasoning tests three forms of logical reasoning and reveals substantial, uneven weaknesses in leading multimodal models.

paragraphs: Long recordings can contain rare, meaningful sounds surrounded by dominant background patterns. Audio language models may struggle to allocate attention to those events. NAACA addresses this as a filtering problem: determine when the audio becomes perceptually salient, then invoke the language model for higher-level processing. The architecture operates without additional training.

Its central component is Oscillatory Working Memory, a neuro-inspired mechanism that maintains stable, attractor-like states. Adaptive changes in its energy signal when incoming audio warrants further attention. This gives the system a persistent state for monitoring sound and a trigger for escalating selected moments to the audio language model, linking event sensitivity with selective computation.

On XD-Violence, NAACA increases AudioQwen’s average precision from 53.50% to 70.60% while reducing unnecessary model invocations. Qualitative studies on Urban Soundscapes of the World show detection of novel events and shifts between subcategories, alongside robustness to short pauses and ambient noise. The quantitative result supports the evaluated detection improvement, while the urban examples illustrate how the memory mechanism responds to changing soundscapes.
icml-2026-naaca-training-free-neuroaudit.tldr: NAACA uses oscillatory working memory to trigger audio-model reasoning at salient moments, improving detection while reducing unnecessary invocations.

paragraphs: The maximal coding rate reduction objective, MCR², supports learning representations organized into low-dimensional subspaces. It can also guide neural-network design by turning optimization steps into layers. The paper argues that existing designs inspired by this objective do not fully follow the implications of its gradient, weakening the connection between the mathematical principle and the resulting architecture.

PACEAttention uses the geometry of that gradient to guide feature updates. The relevant directions depend on the low-dimensional structure within the features, and the mechanism uses randomization to capture that structure. Its attention design is therefore tied to how the objective suggests features should move, providing a more explicit basis for interpreting the computation.

The resulting PACENet develops attention heads that focus on distinct image regions and capture fine-grained structures under simple supervised training. Experiments show better performance and more stable scaling than previous principled modules while retaining low complexity. These findings connect the proposed geometric construction with both useful visual organization and empirical performance, within the comparisons reported by the authors.
icml-2026-paceattention-principled-and-a.tldr: PACEAttention uses MCR² geometry and randomized structure estimation to build efficient attention with interpretable visual features.

paragraphs: Predicting cellular responses is difficult because single-cell sequencing destroys the measured cell. Researchers therefore observe separate control and perturbed populations rather than matched before-and-after measurements. Many models learn a mapping between these populations while assuming one response distribution for a given observed cell context and perturbation. The paper argues that hidden factors create systematic variation beyond that assumption.

PerturbDiff models entire response distributions as the objects that vary. It embeds probability distributions as points in a Hilbert space and defines a diffusion-based generative process over those points. This allows the same observed conditions to correspond to multiple possible population-level responses, accounting for variability associated with unobserved influences such as microenvironmental changes and complex batch effects.

The approach aims to capture shifts in the response population itself, rather than only variation among cells within one fixed response distribution. Benchmarks on established datasets show state-of-the-art single-cell response prediction and substantially better generalization to unseen perturbations. The results support representing uncertainty and variability at the distribution level when learning how cell populations respond.
icml-2026-perturbdiff-functional-diffusi.tldr: PerturbDiff generates distributions of cellular responses to capture hidden population-level variability and improve prediction of unseen perturbations.

paragraphs: Converting artificial neural networks into spiking networks offers a route to spiking language models without additional training. Existing conversion pipelines mainly support the linear algebra inside Transformers. Important nonlinear operations remain difficult because division, exponentiation, and norm calculations do not fit naturally into standard leaky integrate-and-fire neuron dynamics.

The proposed framework builds spike-friendly approximations from three reusable primitives: division, exponentiation, and L2 norms. Groups of leaky integrate-and-fire neurons perform population computations, with lightweight bit shifts handling scaling without floating-point arithmetic. Composing these primitives yields modular replacements for nonlinear operations such as Softmax, SiLU, and normalization, and the blocks integrate into existing conversion pipelines.

These replacements require no fine-tuning, making them useful components for extending the operations supported by conversion. Experiments across a range of language-model Transformers find less than a 1% accuracy drop on every evaluated task when selected nonlinear operators are replaced. The reported result concerns those selective replacements, supporting the accuracy of the proposed operator approximations within the tested settings.
icml-2026-plug-and-play-spiking-operator.tldr: Modular spiking approximations extend Transformer conversion to key nonlinear operators with less than a 1% accuracy drop in the evaluated tasks.

paragraphs: Poster design requires coordinating visual appearance with the order and prominence of information. The paper describes two shortcomings of existing approaches: text-to-image generation struggles with precise text and editability, while layout-generation systems often produce a single fixed prediction. A one-shot process lacks an explicit mechanism for revising a draft after problems become apparent.

PosterAgent organizes creation into an initial drafting stage followed by repeated refinement. To train this multi-turn workflow, Stage-Aware Reinforcement Learning separates optimization for drafting from optimization for revision. This makes credit assignment specific to the kind of action being learned: creating a useful starting point and making a useful incremental change are treated as distinct training responsibilities.

The distinction matters because a successful final poster depends on both stages of the process. Training them separately gives the framework an explicit way to develop initial composition and subsequent self-correction. Extensive experiments show significant improvements over strong baselines. The reported findings support the potential of iterative agents for graphic design and the value of training the stages of their workflow deliberately.
icml-2026-posteragent-agentic-poster-gen.tldr: PosterAgent learns poster drafting and iterative refinement through separate reinforcement-learning stages, outperforming strong baselines.

paragraphs: Quantization reduces the precision of language-model weights, while low-rank adapters provide a compact way to fine-tune them. Applying these methods sequentially can create a mismatch: quantization errors may be spread across weight directions that a low-rank adapter cannot easily repair. The adapter then spends limited capacity compensating for compression instead of adapting to the downstream task.

ProjQ shapes quantization noise to fit the structure the adapter can handle. An alternating algorithm uses orthogonal subspace projection to concentrate dominant error components into a low-rank structure while minimizing error in the remaining, uncorrectable subspace. The theoretical analysis establishes strictly greater downstream model plasticity than standard post-training quantization, formalizing the benefit of preserving more capacity for adaptation.

Experiments on LLaMA-2, Qwen2.5, and Qwen3 show consistent improvements in error compensation and downstream fine-tuning. Reported gains include up to twofold lower compensation evaluation loss and language-modeling performance matching standard 4-bit baselines with 3-bit weights. These results support designing compression around the subsequent adapter’s capabilities, rather than treating the two stages independently.
icml-2026-projq-project-and-quantize-for.tldr: ProjQ shapes quantization errors into directions low-rank adapters can repair, preserving capacity for downstream learning.

paragraphs: Forecasting from few time-series examples creates a risk that a model memorizes limited training data instead of learning patterns that generalize. ReAugment addresses this by learning both where augmentation is most useful and how to transform the selected examples. Its augmentation process is targeted using information from several forecasting models.

The framework maintains a model zoo and measures diversity among its predictions to identify samples considered especially prone to overfitting. Those samples become anchors for augmentation. A reinforcement-learning policy then chooses transformations, guided by a reward derived from the model zoo. The reward steers generated data toward overfit-prone regions where augmentation is expected to help generalization.

Using reinforcement learning avoids the need to backpropagate gradients through the forecasting models, mitigating vanishing-gradient problems in the augmentation process. Experiments across diverse forecasting architectures demonstrate effectiveness in both few-shot and standard forecasting settings. The results support using model disagreement to focus augmentation effort and a learned transformation policy to make that effort useful across different predictors.
icml-2026-reaugment-targeted-few-shot-ti.tldr: ReAugment uses forecasting-model disagreement and reinforcement learning to target data augmentation where it can improve generalization.

paragraphs: Spatial proteomics measures protein expression at single-cell resolution while retaining information about tissue organization. Its analysis can require experts to coordinate many different tools, from processing multiplexed tissue images to discovering cellular phenotypes. The paper identifies this fragmented workflow as an obstacle to scaling research and making analyses reproducible.

SP-Mind brings these steps into an autonomous agent that turns natural-language requests into end-to-end analytical workflows. It combines expert-curated biological analysis skills with specialized computational tools and requires no task-specific fine-tuning. The system’s contribution lies in coordinating the pipeline, allowing the request and available expertise to guide a connected sequence of analytical operations.

The authors introduce SP-Bench to evaluate this capability across diverse tissues, with 102 tasks in 18 categories. Evaluations on that benchmark and established downstream tasks report state-of-the-art performance relative to existing open-source biomedical agents. These findings support the effectiveness of the integrated workflow for the evaluated analysis tasks, connecting natural-language interaction with specialized spatial proteomics computation.
icml-2026-sp-mind-an-autonomous-reasonin.tldr: SP-Mind coordinates spatial proteomics tools into natural-language-driven workflows and outperforms evaluated open-source biomedical agents.

paragraphs: Sparse time-series regression seeks a small set of useful lags or factors, making a model easier to interpret and potentially cheaper to compute. An L0 constraint directly limits how many coefficients are nonzero. Although such methods work well empirically, their statistical and computational behavior is less established when observations are dependent over time.

The paper studies least-squares regression for stationary Gaussian processes with sparse coefficients and alpha-mixing dependence. Under this setting, it establishes high-probability restricted strong convexity and smoothness for the empirical loss. These properties describe the loss geometry over sparse directions and support finite-sample statistical guarantees and computational complexity results for methods including iterative hard thresholding.

The theory also yields new guarantees for Gaussian vector autoregressive models. Experiments on synthetic sparse autoregressive systems and real mobility data show more accurate and interpretable lag recovery than some classical methods, with comparable prediction error and substantially lower computational cost. The contribution joins these empirical benefits with guarantees that explicitly account for temporal dependence under the stated process assumptions.
icml-2026-sparse-regression-with-ell-0-c.tldr: The paper establishes finite-sample and computational guarantees for exact sparse regression under specified dependent Gaussian time-series assumptions.

paragraphs: Training software-engineering agents with reinforcement learning requires environments in which tasks can execute in isolation. Container-based pipelines can become expensive when many task instances require pre-cached images. Their storage demands constrain resource-limited training, and the need for container-management privileges can prevent some users from running the infrastructure at all.

SWE-MiniSandbox replaces per-instance containers with isolated workspaces supported by kernel-level mechanisms. Lightweight environment pre-caching removes the need to store bulky container images. The method retains task isolation while reducing the infrastructure associated with preparing and keeping many environments, addressing a practical bottleneck in scaling agent training.

The reported implementation uses approximately 5% of the disk space required by container-based pipelines and takes about 25% of their environment preparation time. Evaluation performance remains comparable to standard container-based training. These findings show that substantial savings in environment overhead can coexist with similar evaluated agent performance, making the approach relevant to research settings where storage, preparation costs, or container privileges are limiting factors.
icml-2026-swe-minisandbox-container-free.tldr: SWE-MiniSandbox uses kernel-backed isolated workspaces to cut training-environment overhead while maintaining comparable agent performance.

paragraphs: Off-policy reinforcement learning can overestimate how valuable an action is. The paper connects this bias to total value uncertainty and argues that existing methods focus too heavily on epistemic uncertainty, associated with incomplete knowledge. Neglecting aleatoric uncertainty, associated with randomness in returns, can allow a brief but large bias surge that the authors call an Aleatoric Impulse.

The authors find that this transient surge can derail learning and lock an agent into a suboptimal policy. Aleatoric Impulse Damping separates return variance into epistemic and aleatoric components, then recombines them with adaptive weights. The critic uses the resulting uncertainty to form a pessimistic lower confidence bound that suppresses excessive value estimates.

The actor uses a corresponding optimistic upper confidence bound to support exploration, balancing conservative value learning with the incentive to try uncertain actions. Integrating the mechanism into Distributional Soft Actor-Critic produces DSAC-AID. Experiments on high-dimensional Gym-MuJoCo and DeepMind Control Suite tasks report state-of-the-art final performance, supporting the value of addressing both uncertainty components in the tested control settings.
icml-2026-taming-aleatoric-impulse-in-of.tldr: AID separates and recombines two sources of value uncertainty to suppress damaging overestimation surges while supporting exploration.

paragraphs: Multimodal language-model architectures face a trade-off between training and inference costs. The paper contrasts embedding-space alignment, which is inefficient during inference, with cross-attention alignment, which is inefficient during training. It investigates a key architectural difference: whether visual tokens themselves attend to other tokens inside the language-model backbone.

The authors first introduce NAEViT, an attention mechanism that removes interactions originating from visual tokens. A pilot experiment indicates that these interactions are highly redundant. Building on that finding, SAISA aligns visual features directly with the input spaces of NAEViT attention blocks. This reduces work in both attention and feed-forward networks, addressing computation in two parts of the model.

Experiments span different baseline models, model sizes, and training datasets. SAISA achieves better performance than the evaluated baselines while substantially reducing computational costs, and ablations support its effectiveness across different language models and visual encoders. The findings suggest that the studied visual-token interactions can be removed within this design while improving the balance between training efficiency, inference efficiency, and predictive performance.
icml-2026-towards-multimodal-large-langu.tldr: SAISA removes redundant visual-token attention and aligns visual features directly to attention inputs, improving performance and computational efficiency.

paragraphs: Poisoned fine-tuning data can implant backdoors in language models, but the internal mechanisms that carry those behaviors are difficult to inspect. BkdAttr studies those mechanisms through a three-part causal analysis. Its first component, the Backdoor Probe, establishes that model representations contain learnable features associated with the backdoor.

Backdoor Attention Head Attribution then identifies the attention heads responsible for processing those features. In the primary experiments, these heads are relatively sparse: ablating approximately 3% of all heads is sufficient to reduce attack success rate by more than 90%. This result localizes substantial backdoor functionality to a small portion of the tested models’ attention machinery.

The authors also derive a Backdoor Vector from the attributed heads. A single intervention on one representation can drive attack success on clean inputs to approximately 100%, or suppress it on triggered inputs to approximately zero in the reported experiments. Together, attribution, ablation, and vector intervention provide evidence for controllable internal backdoor mechanisms, beyond simply observing whether a trigger changes a model’s output.
icml-2026-uncovering-hidden-triggers-bac.tldr: BkdAttr identifies sparse attention heads involved in backdoors and derives representation interventions that strongly control attack success in experiments.
